teaser.text: Lowe’s is a home-improvement retailer: it sells the goods people use to repair, maintain, improve and build homes, and it arranges some of the work. Its business becomes clearer when you follow the dollar from a shopper or professional buyer to suppliers, installers, employees and the profit left over.

stock.title: Lowe’s stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Lowe’s weighted forecast reaches $269.07 by October 2029, with bear, base and bull cases tied to cash generation, debt and execution.
stock.opening: Lowe’s weighted forecast reaches $269.07 by October 2029, with a 52% base case between a 30% bear case and an 18% bull case. It hinges on whether acquired businesses become profitable enough to support cash generation and debt reduction.
stock.closing: The full memo also explains Lowe’s business, rivals, management and risks.

blocks.heading: Where could Lowe’s shares be by October 2029?

paragraphs.text: The forecast puts Lowe’s weighted share value at $210.68 in October 2027, up 10% with dividends, and $238.63 in October 2028, up 27%. By October 2029, the weighted value reaches $269.07, a 45% total return from today’s $196.33.

The range is much wider than the weighted path suggests. The bear case ends at $156.77, while the bull case reaches $394.90. The probabilities are 30% bear, 52% base and 18% bull because stabilization appears more likely than either a prolonged downturn or a rapid housing recovery.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Lowe’s stock forecast?

paragraphs.text: Operating profit is the central earnings driver. The base case rises from $10,602 million in October 2027 to $11,880 million in October 2029. The starting point is above the latest full-year result because management’s guide implies roughly $10.3 billion of operating income, while the base assumes modestly stronger sales and margin. The final margin reaches 12.0%, still below the five-year 12.6% average. The bear case keeps margins near 10.5% to 10.8% as transactions remain weak; the bull case reaches 12.5% as housing, Pro demand and integration improve. Eight recent earnings beats support execution confidence, but only four revenue beats and the acquired segment’s $70 million operating loss argue against a rapid recovery.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Lowe’s really make?

paragraphs.text: After $2,213 million of capital spending, free cash flow was $7,651 million. That is cash after investment in long-lived assets, not cash available after acquisitions, dividends and debt repayments. Deducting $247 million of stock compensation gives an analytical “real free cash flow” measure, because issuing shares to employees still dilutes owners even though it is not another cash payment that year.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Lowe’s today?

paragraphs.text: At $196.33 a share, Lowe’s equity is worth $110,151.74 million. Its 16.6x trailing P/E, or price-to-earnings ratio, means investors pay $16.60 for each dollar earned recently; the 15.1x forward P/E uses expected earnings instead. EPS must still be checked against total profit because buybacks can make each remaining share claim more of unchanged earnings. Imagine $100 million of profit spread across ten shares. Each share then represents $10. If Lowe’s buys back half the shares, the same profit produces higher EPS, although the business has not earned more.

dividend.closing: The full memo also covers Lowe’s business, rivals, management, and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does Lowe’s pay per share?

paragraphs.text: The base dividend rises from $5.00 per share to $5.40. The latest declared quarterly rate supports the first year, while the five-year record of increases supports modest growth thereafter. The bear case freezes the annualized rate at $5.00; the bull case reaches $5.62 as cash generation improves. Free cash flow covered dividends comfortably in fiscal 2025.

blocks.heading: Is Lowe’s dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: The position changed in the year ended January 2026. Free cash flow was $7,651 million and dividends were $2,636 million. Buybacks were only $211 million, leaving $4,804 million before acquisitions and other movements. Acquisition spending reached $10,088 million, so Lowe’s issued $6,974 million of debt and repaid $2,587 million. Net debt rose to $38,569 million from $33,354 million.

paragraphs.text: The bull case would gain weight if housing turnover and big-ticket projects lift transactions during 2027 and 2028, while Pro service gains make FBM and ADG profitable. Faster cash generation, progress toward the mid-2027 leverage target and renewed buybacks would then support higher earnings and a wider multiple.

blocks.heading: What is Lowe’s dividend yield today?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow offers another lens. Its 6.9% yield compares favourably with a 5.22% ten-year US government-bond yield, but Lowe’s definition subtracts ordinary capital spending, not the purchase price of an entire company. Inventory also absorbs cash before the spring selling season. The 2.5% dividend yield is only one use of that cash, while the 6.7% real yield depends on how its adjustment is defined.

earnings.title: Lowe’s earnings: guidance and what to watch
earnings.meta_description: Lowe’s next results are expected November 18, 2026; guidance calls for flat comparable sales and adjusted diluted earnings per share of $12.25.
earnings.opening: Lowe’s next results are expected on November 18, 2026. Watch comparable sales, transactions and the annual outlook together.
earnings.closing: The full memo also answers questions about Lowe’s business, its rivals, its management and its risks.

blocks.heading: What has Lowe’s guided for the year ending January 2027?

paragraphs.text: On August 19, 2026, management guided to sales of $92,000 million and flat comparable sales for the year ending January 2027. Comparable sales measure the established business: an existing store selling the same amount as last year has flat comparable sales. Total sales can still rise through new stores, online growth or acquisitions such as FBM and ADG.

Management guided to adjusted diluted earnings per share of $12.25. Operating margin, which shows the share of sales left after operating costs, is guided to 11.2%, while adjusted operating margin is 11.6%. Reported diluted earnings per share are $11.75 because reported profit includes acquisition-related intangible-asset amortization. That accounting expense spreads the value assigned to acquired customer relationships and other assets across their useful lives; it is not a new quarterly cash payment.

blocks.heading: What is the trend in Lowe’s last eight quarters?

paragraphs.text: Revenue rose 8.3% to $25,956 million, while comparable sales increased only 0.2%. Professional customers, home services and online orders helped. Comparable transactions fell 2.1%, while ticket rose 2.3%. That again suggests larger purchases offset fewer visits.

Profit barely followed sales. Operating income rose to $3,549 million, but gross margin fell to 33.0% and net income was essentially unchanged at $2,399 million. Acquired-business mix, fuel costs and higher interest reduced the benefit of added revenue.

blocks.heading: What should I watch in Lowe’s next results?

paragraphs.text: The next earnings release, estimated for November 18, 2026, should be read through three measures together: comparable sales, transactions and the annual outlook. More revenue from higher prices differs from more customers buying, and another earnings beat matters less if management cuts its full-year promise again.
